answer: The passage says DeepWalk can be viewed as a generalization of neural language models because it uses the same core idea: learn vector representations by predicting nearby context from a sequence. In a neural language model, the sequence is ordinary text and the model learns word embeddings from word co-occurrence in sentences. DeepWalk applies that same skip-gram-style idea to random walks on a graph, treating the walk as a sentence and the nodes as words. The special language it processes is the "language" of random walks over graph vertices, i.e., sequences of nodes generated by walking the graph.
